samf-senior-2016-r1-02.title: Common denominator 60
samf-senior-2016-r1-02.body:
$\frac12+\frac14+\frac16+\frac1{10}+\frac1{12}=\frac{30+15+10+6+5}{60}=\frac{66}{60}=1+\frac1{10}$. The excess over $1$ is $\frac1{10}$, which is one of the terms: remove it.

**Answer: (D) $\frac1{10}$**

samf-senior-2016-r1-03.title: Prime factorisation
samf-senior-2016-r1-03.body:
$2016=2^5\cdot3^2\cdot7$. For a perfect square every prime must have an even exponent, so the multiplier must supply (at least) one more $2$ and one $7$: $2\cdot7=14$ works, giving $2^6\cdot3^2\cdot7^2=(8\cdot3\cdot7)^2=168^2$. None of the other options contains the factor $7$.

**Answer: (B) 14**

samf-senior-2016-r1-05.title: Chase angles
samf-senior-2016-r1-05.body:
$YT=YR$ gives $\angle YRT=\angle YTR=36^\circ$. So $\angle SRT=24^\circ+36^\circ=60^\circ$. $ST=SR$ gives $\angle STR=\angle SRT=60^\circ$, so $\angle TSR=180^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=60^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $60^\circ$**

samf-senior-2016-r1-06.title: Take n, n+1, n+2
samf-senior-2016-r1-06.body:
The difference between the largest and the smallest is $(n+2)-n=2$, and its square is $4$.

**Answer: (C) 4**

samf-senior-2016-r1-07.title: Convert through rand
samf-senior-2016-r1-07.body:
One pound is R21 and R12 is one dollar, so one pound is $\frac{21}{12}=1.75$ dollars.

**Answer: (E) 1.75**

samf-senior-2016-r1-08.title: Try the largest counts
samf-senior-2016-r1-08.body:
Write $34=3a+5b+7c$ and maximise $a$. $a=10$ leaves $4$, which cannot be made from $5$s and $7$s. $a=11$ leaves $1$, impossible. Larger $a$ exceeds $34$. $a=9$ leaves $7=7\cdot1$: $9\times3+7=34$ works.

**Answer: (D) 9**

samf-senior-2016-r1-10.title: Count favourable books
samf-senior-2016-r1-10.body:
There are $64-24=40$ such books out of $1024$: $\frac{40}{1024}=\frac5{128}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac5{128}$**

samf-senior-2016-r1-12.title: Equation
samf-senior-2016-r1-12.body:
After $x$ years: $45+x=2(17+x)$, so $x=11$ and the year is $2016+11=2027$.

**Answer: (E) 2027**

samf-senior-2016-r1-12.title: Age difference
samf-senior-2016-r1-12.body:
The age difference stays $45-17=28$ years. She is double his age exactly when he is $28$. He is $17$ now, so this happens in $11$ years: $2027$.

**Answer: (E) 2027**

samf-senior-2016-r1-13.title: Area of the line
samf-senior-2016-r1-13.body:
The line covers $0.4\times10^{-3}\text{ m}\times10^3\text{ m}=0.4\text{ m}^2$, and the same ink colours a square of that area.

**Answer: (E) 0.4**

samf-senior-2016-r1-15.title: Parity pattern
samf-senior-2016-r1-15.body:
Parities: odd, odd, then odd+odd=even, odd+even=odd, even+odd=odd, odd+odd=even, ... The pattern odd, odd, even repeats every $3$ terms. Each cycle contributes remainders $1+1+0=2$. There are $2016/3=672$ cycles, so the sum is $672\times2=1344$.

**Answer: (C) 1 344**

samf-senior-2016-r1-17.title: Count multiples
samf-senior-2016-r1-17.body:
The multiples of $13$ up to $169$ are $13,26,\dots,169$: that is $13$ numbers, each contributing one factor $13$, and $169=13^2$ contributes one extra. Total $14$.

**Answer: (C) 14**

samf-senior-2016-r1-18.title: Use the side length
samf-senior-2016-r1-18.body:
Let the side be $s$. Then $AB=2s$ and $CD=s\sqrt3$ (twice the apothem $\frac{\sqrt3}2s$), so $AB\times CD=2\sqrt3\,s^2$. The area of the hexagon is $\frac{3\sqrt3}2s^2=126$, so $\sqrt3\,s^2=84$ and $AB\times CD=168$.

**Answer: (D) 168**

samf-senior-2016-r1-18.title: Compare areas
samf-senior-2016-r1-18.body:
Cut the hexagon into $6$ congruent equilateral triangles. The rectangle with sides $AB$ and $CD$ around the hexagon also contains four right triangles which fit together into $2$ more such equilateral triangles. So its area is $\frac86\times126=168$, and this equals $AB\times CD$.

**Answer: (D) 168**

samf-senior-2016-r1-19.title: Gold balance
samf-senior-2016-r1-19.body:
The mixture has $0.5$ g of gold. Adding $x$ g gives $\dfrac{0.5+x}{5+x}=0.2$, so $0.5+x=1+0.2x$, $0.8x=0.5$ and $x=0.625$.

**Answer: (E) 0.625**

samf-senior-2016-r1-19.title: Other metal stays the same
samf-senior-2016-r1-19.body:
The other metal is $4.5$ g, and it must become $80\%$ of the new total, so the total is $4.5/0.8=5.625$ g and $5.625-5=0.625$ g of gold was added.

**Answer: (E) 0.625**

samf-senior-2016-r1-20.title: Trigonometry
samf-senior-2016-r1-20.body:
Let $\angle CBF=\angle EBF=\theta$, $x$ the side of the square. From $\triangle BCF$: $\tan\theta=3/x$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle AEB=\angle EBC=2\theta$, and in $\triangle BAE$, $\tan2\theta=x/2$. With $\tan2\theta=\frac{2t}{1-t^2}$, $t=3/x$: $\frac x2=\frac{6x}{x^2-9}$, so $x^2-9=12$, $x^2=21$ and $EB^2=x^2+4=25$, $EB=5$.

**Answer: (B) 5**

samf-senior-2016-r1-20.title: Rotation
samf-senior-2016-r1-20.body:
Rotate $\triangle BAE$ by $90^\circ$ about $B$ so that $A$ goes to $C$ and $E$ to $E'$ on line $DC$ extended beyond $C$, with $CE'=AE=2$ and $BE'=BE$. Now $\angle E'BF=\angle E'BC+\angle CBF=(90^\circ-2\theta)+\theta=90^\circ-\theta$, and $\angle BFE'=\angle BFC=90^\circ-\theta$, so $E'B=E'F=2+3=5$. Hence $EB=5$.

**Answer: (B) 5**
